note: Hoverline sample library. gain brings each recording to its voice's reference loudness (the Prototype 44 kit piece); vel is the velocity range of its layer (0-1); on is where the sound starts and hit where its main transient is (seconds from the start of the file: start it at t - hit to put the attack on the beat); n is its length in samples at sr; root is the MIDI note (may be fractional: measured) for tuned sounds; at is [byte offset, length] in its pack.

sonicpi.name: Sonic Pi sample pack (freesound.org recordings)
sonicpi.credit: Drum hits from the Sonic Pi sample pack (freesound.org uploads by menegass, looppool and others; CC0), as lossless FLAC originals

virtuosity.name: Virtuosity Drums (Versilian Studios with Karoryfer Samples)
virtuosity.credit: Acoustic drums and auxiliary percussion: Virtuosity Drums by Versilian Studios and Karoryfer Samples, played by Austin McMahon (CC0)

vcsl.name: Versilian Community Sample Library
vcsl.credit: Percussion, timpani, concert bass drum, cymbals and didgeridoo: the Versilian Community Sample Library (CC0)

vsco2.name: VSCO-2 Community Edition
vsco2.credit: Orchestral percussion: VSCO-2 Community Edition by Versilian Studios (CC0)

muldjord.name: MuldjordKit (FreePats version) by Lars Muldjord
muldjord.credit: Rock and metal kit: MuldjordKit by Lars Muldjord (FreePats version by Roberto), CC BY 4.0. Drum samples provided by DrumGizmo.org.

fp_hang.name: FreePats Hang tuned in D minor
fp_hang.credit: Hang drum: FreePats "Hang tuned in D minor", played by Mar, recorded by Gonzalo and Roberto (CC0)

fp_egtr.name: FreePats Electric Guitar FSBS
fp_egtr.credit: Electric guitar: FreePats Electric Guitar FSBS (direct, clean, dist1 and dist2 banks, CC0)

fp_bass.name: FreePats Finger Bass YR / Picked Bass YR
fp_bass.credit: Electric bass: FreePats Finger Bass YR and Picked Bass YR by Andrea Biasior (CC0)

fp_world.name: FreePats World percussion
fp_world.credit: Cajon, bongos, shakers, tambourine, castanets, maracas and darbuka: FreePats World percussion, played by Xavimart (CC0)

hoverline.name: Synthesised for Hoverline
hoverline.credit: Electronic drums (808, 909, techno, house, trance, psytrance, hardcore, drum & bass): synthesised offline for Hoverline

808.notes: A TR-808 family, synthesised: a bridged-T kick with a tuned tail (root in the manifest; kick_long rings on F1, kick G1, kick_short A1, kick_dist a saturated one), snare, clap, the six-square metallic hats (soft-topped), cowbell, three toms, rimshot, clave, maracas, and the shared dark crash.

909.notes: A TR-909 family, synthesised: kick with click and pitch sweep (and a longer one), noise snare in three layers, clap, hats with body at 8 kHz and a held-down top, ride, a dark crash, rimshot and toms.

breaks.label: Breaks (tight acoustic)
breaks.notes: Virtuosity Drums mixed tight for re-played amen and Think breaks: close mics with phase-aligned overheads, a little of the vintage "lofi" mic, the snare tuned up a semitone, compressed for punch and run through soft tape saturation. Kick (snares off) 2 layers x 4, snare 3 layers x 4-5 (the soft layer is the ghost note), rimshot, cross-stick, closed, half-open, open and pedal hats, ride, crash, two toms (the mid tom is the high tom tuned down).

concert.label: Concert and orchestral
concert.notes: The concert bass drum Eric liked (VSCO-2, four velocities, round robins): kick (damped to 0.9 s for a kit) and kick_long (the full ring); a second bass drum (kick2), concert snare, rimshot and cross-stick (VCSL), clash cymbals (crash, shelved: Eric found the old one a little sharp), a suspended cymbal (crash2), a swell (fx_swell) and mallet toms.

cym.label: Synth cymbals
cym.notes: Shared synthesised rides (normal and dark, with a bell) and crashes (normal and dark), built from many inharmonic partials, with the top held down. These replace the distorted crash.

didg.label: Didgeridoo
didg.notes: VCSL didgeridoo: two sustained drones (5 s), three rhythmic phrases (4 s), two barks, a short note and a tap. root is the measured drone pitch, so a tune can retune it to its key with playbackRate = 2^((key - root)/12).

dnb.label: Drum & bass (electronic)
dnb.notes: Snares tight and snappy with a 200 Hz body and a crack (snare), a harder crack (snare_crack) and a fatter one (snare_fat), each in three layers (the soft one is the ghost note); a punchy kick with a bright click; soft hats.

electro.label: Electro kit (new top end)
electro.notes: The electro kit's Sonic Pi kicks and low snare (lossless), with a new tight electro snare and the dark synthesised hats in place of the old bright ones Eric disliked.

esn.label: Electro and dub snares
esn.notes: New snares for the gas, electro and tape kits.

funk.label: Funk (natural acoustic)
funk.notes: Virtuosity Drums mixed full and natural: close mics, overheads and the room, uncompressed. Ghost notes, cross-stick, half-open hats and a ride bell for funk and liquid grooves.

gas.label: Gas kit (new snare)
gas.notes: The gas kit's kicks (lossless) with a new dark, round dub snare in place of the one Eric disliked on 2 and 4, and dark hats.

hand.label: Hand drums
hand.notes: Frame drums and hand drums, open and muted, large and small (VCSL; the nearest CC0 thing to a djembe here), darbuka doum, tek and pa, cajon bass and slap, maracas (back and forward strokes), castanets and real hand claps (FreePats World percussion); the shaker and tambourine are the latin kit's.

hardcore.label: Hardcore
hardcore.notes: Gabber kick (overdriven until it is a tone, settling on its root) and a lighter happy-hardcore kick, both with their root note in the manifest, a hard bright snare, a big clap, 909 hats and a crash.

hats.label: Soft and dark hats
hats.notes: Shared hats for the electronic kits: closed and open in soft, dark and tape colours, a pedal chick, the short offbeat open hats for trance and psytrance, an egg shaker (forward and back strokes) and a finger snap.

house.label: House
house.notes: A round, warm house kick, a 909-ish snare with a long soft wire, a roomy clap, soft hats, egg shaker and ride.

jazz.label: Jazz (sticks)
jazz.notes: Virtuosity Drums as a jazz kit (it is one): overhead-led with the room, close mics low, the softer layers, the ride with its bell, a flat ride, a sizzle crash, cross-stick and a snares-off snare. Played with sticks: no CC0 brush recordings were reachable.

latin.label: Latin percussion
latin.notes: Congas (open in two layers, heel-muted), tumba, high and low bongos, timbales, cowbell, claves, agogo, shaker (up and down strokes as two layers) and tambourine: the VSCO 2 Pro and Karoryfer percussion that ships with Virtuosity Drums.

original.label: Original kit (lossless)
original.notes: The Prototype 25 kit from its lossless FLAC originals: bd_tek, sn_dolf and sn_zome, the menegass acoustic hits. Each hit has 3-4 round robins derived from the one recording. The bright closed hat (drum_cymbal_closed) is shelved above 10 kHz.

psy.label: Psytrance
psy.notes: A very short, tight kick with a clear click (gone before the next 16th of bass), a crisp clap and snap, dark closed hats and a very short offbeat open hat.

rock.label: Rock and metal (MuldjordKit)
rock.notes: MuldjordKit, a rock/metal kit recorded by Lars Muldjord (CC BY 4.0, credit: "Drum samples provided by DrumGizmo.org"). kick alternates the left and right kick drums (a real double pedal); snare 3 layers; closed hats 3 layers; crash, china, ride and bell; four toms (tomF is the floor tom).

tabla.label: Tabla (lossless)
tabla.notes: The Sonic Pi tabla strokes from their FLAC originals: ghe (bayan bass, 8 takes), ke, te, na (open, slap, other), tun, tas, re, dhe. The takes of one stroke are its round robins.

tape.label: Tape kit (new top end)
tape.notes: The tape kit's kicks and filtered snare (lossless), with the new tape-coloured hats (dark, rolled off above 9 kHz).

techno.label: Techno
techno.notes: Kicks: clean (909-like, long and round), industrial (driven hard, asymmetric, gritty mids) and rumble-ready (short, dry and deep, no tail of its own, to feed a reverb and low-pass rumble). 909 snare, clap, hats, ride and rim.

tight.label: Tight kit (lossless)
tight.notes: The tight kit Eric liked for psytrance (bd_zum, bd_pure, sn_generic), lossless. Its open hat (hat_gump, the likely "tsshh") is left out: the open hat comes from the soft synthesised hats instead.

trance.label: Trance
trance.notes: A tight, punchy kick with a knock around 80 Hz, a layered clap, a noise snare for rolls, soft closed hats and a short soft offbeat open hat (body at 7 kHz, closes quickly) instead of the old "tsshh".

bass_finger.label: Finger bass
bass_finger.notes: FreePats Finger Bass YR (a Yamaha RBX): one note per semitone from E1 to D#2; higher notes retune the top ones.

bass_pick.label: Picked bass
bass_pick.notes: FreePats Picked Bass YR: every other semitone from E1 to E2.

gtr_chug.label: Palm-muted single notes
gtr_chug.notes: Single low notes, palm-muted, through the same amp: the tight metal chug.

gtr_clean.label: Clean guitar (notes)
gtr_clean.notes: FreePats Electric Guitar FSBS, clean bank: every other recorded note (retuned by a semitone or two between).

gtr_dist.label: Distorted guitar (notes)
gtr_dist.notes: FreePats Electric Guitar FSBS, dist1 bank (bridge pickup): every other recorded note from C2 to A#5 (distorted notes retune cleanly by a semitone or two).

gtr_mute.label: Power chords (palm-muted)
gtr_mute.notes: Palm-muted power chords (the strings damped at the bridge: fast decay, less top), three round robins, for chugs. Built from the DI notes: FreePats has no recorded palm mutes.

gtr_power.label: Power chords (open)
gtr_power.notes: Root, fifth and octave from the FSBS direct recordings, strummed a few ms apart, through a high-gain amp and 4x12 cabinet rendered offline at 8x. Roots E2, G2, A#2, C#3.

hang.label: Hang drum (D minor)
hang.notes: FreePats Hang in D minor: A3 D4 E4 F4 G4 A4 Bb4 C5 D5 (C4 is not in the bank), two round robins each. Each zone covers only its own note: play the hang in D minor (or retune whole phrases), since every note carries the others ringing in sympathy.

timpani.label: Timpani
timpani.notes: Five timpani from VSCO-2, two round robins each; roots are measured (principal tone), so zone() retunes exactly.

timpani_roll.label: Timpani rolls
timpani_roll.notes: A roll on each of the five timpani, for builds.
